facts: [L1] A linear Lorentz map is a linear $L:V\to V$ with $\eta(Lv,Lw)=\eta(v,w)$ for all $v,w$; it is proper when $\det L=+1$ and orthochronous when $L(C^+)=C^+$ ([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]).

[L2] A spatial rotation of the frame is a linear $R:V\to V$ with $R(e_0)=e_0$, $R(S)\subseteq S$, $\delta(Rw,Rz)=\delta(w,z)$ on the spatial three-space $S$, and $\det(R|_S)=+1$ in $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]).
[L3] The extension $\widehat R=\operatorname{diag}(1,R)$ of a spatial rotation $R$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map ([[lem-boost-rotation-factorization]]).

[L4] For every $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ the passive boost satisfies $B(\boldsymbol\beta)e_0=\gamma(e_0-\beta_1e_1-\beta_2e_2-\beta_3e_3)$ and $B(\mathbf 0)=\operatorname{id}_V$; the map $\boldsymbol\beta\mapsto B(\boldsymbol\beta)e_0$ is injective ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[L1] Killing equation ([[thm-sr-smooth-local-herglotz-noether]], [F10] and steps 9.1, 10.1 there): for a smooth future unit timelike field $n$ with expansion $\theta$, acceleration one-form $a^\flat$ and the Lie derivative of the metric, $\mathcal L_n\eta=2\theta-\bigl(n^\flat\otimes a^\flat+a^\flat\otimes n^\flat\bigr)$; and for a positive smooth $f$, $\mathcal L_{fn}\eta=f\mathcal L_n\eta+df\otimes n^\flat+n^\flat\otimes df$, so $\mathcal L_{fn}\eta=0$ if and only if $\nabla_a(fn)_b+\nabla_b(fn)_a=0$.
direct_context: **Given:** The affine Minkowski space with an inertial chart $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ in which $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and the flat covariant derivative differentiates components ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]]), the kinematics of a congruence with acceleration $a$, expansion $\theta$ and vorticity $\omega$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]]), a length scale $L_0>0$, and the functions and curves of the Construction below.

facts: [F1] The experimental-interface vocabulary: an operational model is a tuple $M=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ with $S$ nonempty, $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ nonempty, $\theta:S\to\Theta$ surjective, $D$ assigning run descriptions and $F:\Theta\to\mathbb R^d$ a prediction map whose components are required, by the declared interpretation $(*)$, to be numbers the framework assigns to $D(s)$ with every intermediate quantity, frame, event, sign and unit declared; a data record $R=(N,z,\varepsilon,a)$ declares that each value lies in the closed box $\prod_j[z_{k,j}-\varepsilon_{k,j},z_{k,j}+\varepsilon_{k,j}]$ in the declared units; and clause (f) makes a consistency or comparison claim between a record and a model a separate claim requiring an explicitly declared comparison rule ([[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]]).

[F2] Doppler theorem clauses (i) and (ii): for inertial charts whose transition is $x'=B(\beta)x+b$ with $\beta\in\mathbb R^3$, $|\beta|<1$, the same future null wave covector $k$ with frame-$x$ data $(\omega,s)$ has frame-$x'$ data $(\omega',s')$ with $\omega'=\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\omega$, where $\gamma=(1-|\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$; and the rest observers of $x$ and $x'$, of four-velocities $c e_0$ and $c e'_0$, read the angular frequencies $\omega=-c k(e_0)$ and $\omega'=-c k(e'_0)$ ([[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]]).

[F3] Observer angular frequency and wave data: the observer of four-velocity $U_o=c n$, with $\eta(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ future, reads $\omega_n:=-c k(n)=-k(U_o)$ in the SI convention $x^0=ct$; a future null wave covector has frame components $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ with $\omega>0$ and $|s|=1$ ([[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]]).

[F4] Frame-data lemma clauses (a),(b),(e): for a future null wave covector in a frame, $\varpi:=-k(e_0)>0$ and $|s|=1$; conversely, a covector whose frame components are $(-\varpi,\varpi s_1,\varpi s_2,\varpi s_3)$ with $\varpi>0$ and $|s|=1$ is a future null wave covector ([[lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data]]).

[F5] Passive boost: for $\beta$ with $|\beta|<1$ the map $B(\beta)$ is defined in an inertial frame's coordinates by $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta\cdot x)$ and $x'=x+((\gamma-1)/|\beta|^2)(\beta\cdot x)\beta-\gamma\beta x^0$ for $\beta\neq0$, with $B(0)$ the identity, so that in the axis case $\beta=\beta e_1$ one has $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]]); it is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map, $B(\beta)^{-1}=B(-\beta)$, and $B(\beta)e_0=\gamma(e_0-\beta_1 e_1-\beta_2 e_2-\beta_3 e_3)$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[F6] Inertial frame and chart: an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ consists of an event $o\in A$ and an ordered basis of $V$ that is $\eta$-orthonormal, future and positively oriented; its chart is $x(p)=E^{-1}(p-o)$ with $E(u)=\sum_a u^a e_a$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[A1] Adopted ideal plane-wave model: an ideal monochromatic light wave in vacuum is modeled in any inertial chart by a dimensionless affine phase with future null wave covector, and an ideal observer of four-velocity $U_o=c n$ receiving this wave reads the frequency $\omega_n=-c k(n)$ ([[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]]).

[F7] SI conventions: in every inertial chart $x^0=ct$ with $c>0$ in metres per second, spatial coordinates in metres, and the matrix of $\eta$ equal to $\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]).

1.1 Fix $\omega>0$ and let $k$ be the covector whose frame-$x$ components are $(-\omega/c,\omega/c,0,0)$, so $\varpi=\omega/c>0$ and $s=e_1$ with $|s|=1$; by [F4] the covector $k$ is a future null wave covector with frame-$x$ data $(\omega,e_1)$; equip it with the affine phase $\theta(p):=k(p-o)$, whose differential is $k$. For each real $\beta\in(-1,1)$ put $x':=B(\beta e_1)\circ x$ and $f_a:=B(\beta e_1)^{-1}e_a$; by [F5] the map $B(\beta e_1)$ is proper orthochronous with inverse $B(-\beta e_1)$, and [F5] applied to $-\beta e_1$ gives that $B(-\beta e_1)$ also preserves $\eta$, the future cone and the orientation, so the ordered basis $(f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)=(B(-\beta e_1)e_0,\dots,B(-\beta e_1)e_3)$ is again $\eta$-orthonormal, future and positively oriented and $(o;f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)$ is an inertial frame by [F6]; its chart is $x'$, because the frame isomorphism $E_f=E\circ B(\beta e_1)^{-1}$ gives $E_f^{-1}(p-o)=B(\beta e_1)(E^{-1}(p-o))=x'(p)$, and $f_0$ is future unit timelike. facts:
[L1] $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2$ in an $\eta$-orthonormal
basis ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]],
[[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

[L1] A linear map $L$ is a Lorentz map exactly when its matrix $M$ satisfies
$M^{T}\eta_0M=\eta_0$ in the frame's ordered basis; $L$ is proper when
$\det L=1$ and orthochronous when $L(C^+)=C^+$
([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]).

[L2] A Lorentz map satisfies $\det L=\pm1$; $L(C^+)$ is one of the two
components $C^+,C^-$; and $L(C^+)=C^+$ if and only if
$L(C^+)\subseteq C^+$
([[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]]).

[L3] Since $e_0\in C^+$ in an inertial frame, the components are described in
the frame's coordinates by $C^+=\{x:x^0>|x_{\mathrm{vec}}|\}$ and
$C^-=\{x:x^0<-|x_{\mathrm{vec}}|\}$
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

[F1] Slice balance: for $C^1$ $T$, $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$ and a finite axis-parallel box $[s_1,s_2]\times K$, $$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K}f^b\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\Big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^+}T^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^-}T^{ib}\,d^3x\Big),$$ with $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ and $K_i^\pm$ the faces $x^i=d_i$, $x^i=c_i$ of $K$. ([[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]]\,(b))
direct_context: **Given:** An inertial chart $x$ on all of affine Minkowski space with constant metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) and coordinate partial derivatives $\partial_a$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). A field is balanced when its force density $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ vanishes ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]).

facts:
[F3] ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], Definition): an inertial
frame's basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\eta$-orthonormal with $e_0\in C^+$, so
$e_0$ is future timelike and $\eta(e_0,e_0)=-1$.

[F6] ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], Definition):
$E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$ for $P\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$.

[F7] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement (a)): for
nonzero future causal $P$, $E_n(P)>0$ and, for future null $P$,
$E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|$.

[L1] For $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ the passive boost has matrix entries $B^0{}_0=\gamma$, $B^0{}_i=B^i{}_0=-\gamma\beta_i$ and $B^i{}_j=\delta^i{}_j+\frac{\gamma-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^2}\beta_i\beta_j$ in the frame's basis, with $\gamma=(1-|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]]).

[L2] For boosts in a common unit direction $e$ one has $B(\beta_1e)B(\beta_2e)=B\bigl(\frac{\beta_1+\beta_2}{1+\beta_1\beta_2}e\bigr)$ and the two collinear boosts commute ([[lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition]]).

[L3] Every $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map, and products of Lorentz maps are Lorentz maps; the proper orthochronous Lorentz maps form a group ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]], [[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]]).

[L4] The decomposition $L=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$ of a proper orthochronous Lorentz map into a boost and a spatial rotation, with $\boldsymbol\beta=u_{\mathrm{vec}}/u^0$ for $u=Le_0$, is unique, and the rotation factor accounts for the failure of boost products to be boosts ([[lem-boost-rotation-factorization]]).
[L5] Coordinates of the frame are read in the ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[L3] Inertial charts ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]): in an inertial chart the matrix of $\eta$ is $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, so for $v = (v^{0},v^{1},v^{2},v^{3})$ one has $\eta(v,v) = -(v^{0})^{2} + (v^{1})^{2} + (v^{2})^{2} + (v^{3})^{2}$.

[L4] Curves and worldlines ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]): a curve $x(s) = p + s k$ with constant tangent $k$ is $C^{1}$ with $x'(s) = k$; it is a future null curve when $k$ is future null, and a future timelike worldline only when $k$ is future timelike.
[L5] Proper time ([[def-sr-proper-time]]): the proper-time integrand is $\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}$ and the construction is restricted to future timelike worldlines.

[L1] Coordinate criterion and cone description: $q\in J^+(p)$ iff $D^0\ge|D_s|$, and $q\in I^+(p)$ iff $D^0>|D_s|$; a vector $v$ is future null exactly when $|v_s|=v^0>0$ ([[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]]).

[L3] Reachability: $J^+(p)$ and $I^+(p)$ are the causal and chronological futures of $p$ defined by the displacements $q-p\in\overline{C^+}$ and $q-p\in C^+$, and a future timelike worldline is a $C^1$ curve with future timelike tangent everywhere ([[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]).

[L4] Displacement of a future causal path: for a piecewise $C^1$ future causal path with a future timelike one-sided tangent at some point, the displacement lies in $C^+$ ([[thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence]]).

[L1] $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2$ and
$\eta(u,v)=-u^0v^0+u^1v^1+u^2v^2+u^3v^3$ in an $\eta$-orthonormal basis
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

[L1] Pairing in the frame: $\eta(r,r')=-r^0r'^0+r^1r'^1+r^2r'^2+r^3r'^3$ for coordinate vectors, by the diagonal form and bilinearity ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

[L3] Worldlines ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]): a future timelike worldline is a $C^1$ curve all of whose tangents are future timelike; the parametrization is part of the curve, and the image of a future timelike worldline is also the image of the past-directed curve $s\mapsto x(-s)$, which is not a worldline of the model.
[L4] Straight-segment length ([[def-sr-proper-time]]): for a curve with constant tangent $w$ on an interval of length $b-a$, the length integral is $(b-a)\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}$ whenever $w$ is timelike.

[L6] The endpoint bound and its equality case ([[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]]): for a weak piecewise $C^1$ future timelike worldline from $p$ to $q$, $c\Delta\tau\le\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}$ with equality exactly for the strictly increasing reparametrizations of the straight segment; the theorem is stated for future timelike worldlines and attaches no reading to past-directed curves.
direct_context: **Given:** An inertial frame with chart $x$ and $\eta_0=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; the coordinate vector $d=(5,3,0,0)$; the events $p=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)$, $q=x^{-1}(-5,-3,0,0)$; and the curve $x(s)=p-s\,d$ on $[0,1]$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

facts: [F1] Force density and conservation terminology: for a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field $T$, the four-force density is the vector field with components $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$, and $T$ is locally conserved on $\Omega$ exactly when $f=0$ on $\Omega$. ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]])
direct_context: **Given:** The affine Minkowski model with an inertial chart $x$ and coordinate partial derivatives $\partial_a$, an inertial orthonormal frame with $\eta_{ab}=\eta^{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\eta^{ab}=\eta^{ba}$ constant in the chart ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), a nonempty connected open $\Omega\subseteq A$, and $F:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^1$ ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

3.1 Covariance does not imply conservation. Under an inertial transition $x'=\Lambda x+a$ with $\Lambda$ a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), the components of the same tensor transform by the rank-two law $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii)); writing $F'(x'):=F(\Lambda^{-1}(x'-a))$ for the scalar, one gets $T'^{ab}=F'\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_d\eta^{cd}=F'\eta^{ab}$, because $\Lambda\eta^{-1}\Lambda^{\mathsf T}=\eta^{-1}$ for a Lorentz matrix. So the expression $F\eta^{-1}$ is manifestly covariant; yet by step 2.1 its local conservation is equivalent to constancy of the scalar $F$, which covariance does not require. [step 2.1]

facts: [L1] Coordinates and pairing: in the frame's ordered basis $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$, and by bilinearity $\eta(u,u')=-u^0u'^0+u^1u'^1+u^2u'^2+u^3u'^3$ for all $u,u'\in V$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

[L4] The reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and its equality case: for future timelike $v,w$ with $a:=\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}$, $b:=\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}$ one has $-\eta(v,w)\ge ab$, with equality exactly for positive proportional pairs; the same inequality holds for past timelike pairs ([[lem-sr-reverse-cauchy-schwarz-for-future-timelike-vectors]]).
direct_context: **Given:** The oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ and an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with chart $x$ and coordinates $(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3)$ of a vector $u=u^0e_0+u^1e_1+u^2e_2+u^3e_3$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

facts: [L1] Causal classification and orientation: a displacement $w$ is timelike iff $\eta(w,w)<0$, future iff in $C^+$, and in every inertial chart $C^+=\{w:w^0>|w_s|\}$; $p\le q$ iff $q-p\in\bar C^+$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]] (a),(c), [[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]] (a)).
[L2] The affine segment $s\mapsto p+s(q-p)$, $s\in[0,1]$, is a $C^1$ curve of the model whose tangent is the constant displacement $q-p$ ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] (a)).

[L3] Metric and chart: the matrix of $\eta$ in every inertial chart is the constant $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and $\Phi(\theta,\rho,y,z)=(\rho\sinh\theta,\rho\cosh\theta,y,z)$ with $\theta\in\mathbb R$, $\rho>0$ is a smooth bijection onto $W$ with smooth inverse ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (b)).
[L4] Rindler causal criteria: an event $q$ reaches a congruence worldline $\rho=\rho_1$ iff $V(q)<0$, and is reached by it iff $U(q)>0$ ([[pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar]] (ii)).

[L1] Rindler chart and congruence: $U=\rho e^{\theta}$, $V=-\rho e^{-\theta}$; the future null lines in the plane of the two worldlines are the constant-$U$ and constant-$V$ lines; the congruence worldlines have proper acceleration $c^2/\rho$ and Rindler time $\theta=c\tau/\rho$ up to an additive constant ([[pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar]] (i),(ii); [[def-sr-proper-time]]).

[L2] Radar protocol: the radar distance assigned by the observer is $c(\tau(s_+)- \tau(s_-))/2$, half the round-trip proper time of the observer multiplied by $c$, given emission event $e_-$, reflection event $q$, and reception event $e_+$ with $q-e_-$ and $e_+-q$ future null ([[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]]).

[L3] The radar round trip of the coaxial Rindler family: from $O$ at Rindler time $\theta_e$ to the reflector at $\rho_m$, the reflection occurs at $\theta_m=\theta_e+|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ and the return at $\theta_e+2|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$, giving radar distance $\rho_0|\log(\rho_m/\rho_0)|$ for the observer at $\rho_0$ ([[pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar]] (iii)).
[L5] Coordinates and chart: points are determined by their inertial coordinates and $x^0=ct$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[L1] $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ for the inertial frame's basis, so $\eta$ is evaluated on coordinate vectors by $\eta(u,v)=-u^0v^0+u^1v^1+u^2v^2+u^3v^3$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[L2] The future unit timelike vectors are the vectors $n$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$ and $n\in C^+$; the first basis vector $e_0$ of an inertial frame is future unit, and proper orthochronous Lorentz maps preserve the causal classification and the time orientation ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]], [[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]).

[L3] The passive boost with parameter $\beta$, $|\beta|<1$, is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with inverse the boost with parameter $-\beta$, and its matrix in the inertial basis has entries $B^0{}_0=B^1{}_1=\gamma$ and $B^0{}_1=B^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$ on the first two coordinate directions, so $B(-\beta)e_0=\gamma(e_0+\beta e_1)$ for the first basis vector, with $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[L4] For a future unit $n$, $n^\perp=\{v:\eta(n,v)=0\}$ and $H(p,n)=p+n^\perp=\{z:\eta(n,z-p)=0\}$; the slice contains $p$ and is a three-dimensional affine hyperplane ([[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] clause (c), [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).
direct_context: **Given:** The affine Minkowski model with an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and its chart $x$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]), the events $p=x^{-1}(0,0,0,0)=o$ and $q=x^{-1}(0,1,0,0)=o+e_1$, the displacement $d=q-p=e_1$, the future unit vectors $n=e_0$ and $n'=\gamma(e_0+\tfrac35e_1)$ with $\gamma=(1-\tfrac{9}{25})^{-1/2}=\tfrac54$, and the slices $H(p,n)=p+n^\perp$, $H(p,n')=p+n'^\perp$ ([[def-sr-simultaneity-slice-and-rest-distance]]).

facts: [L2] Inertial charts ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]): in an inertial chart the matrix of $\eta$ is $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, so for $v = (v^{0},v^{1},v^{2},v^{3})$ one has $\eta(v,v) = -(v^{0})^{2} + (v^{1})^{2} + (v^{2})^{2} + (v^{3})^{2}$.
[L3] Curves ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]): the curve $x(s) = p + s d$ has constant tangent $x'(s) = d$ and is a future timelike worldline only when $d$ is future timelike.

facts: [L1] For $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ the passive boost has, in the frame's ordered basis, the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}\gamma&-\gamma\boldsymbol\beta^{T}\\ -\gamma\boldsymbol\beta&I_3+\frac{\gamma-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^{2}}\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\beta^{T}\end{pmatrix}$ with $\gamma=(1-|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]]).

[L2] For every $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ the boost $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with $B(\boldsymbol\beta)^{-1}=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$; $B(\boldsymbol\beta)e_0=\gamma(e_0-\beta_1e_1-\beta_2e_2-\beta_3e_3)$; and if $u$ is a future timelike unit vector with coordinates $(u^0,u_{\mathrm{vec}})$, $u^0>0$, then $B(u_{\mathrm{vec}}/u^0)u=e_0$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[L3] For a proper orthochronous Lorentz map $L$ with $u:=Le_0$, coordinates $(u^0,u_{\mathrm{vec}})$, the parameter $\boldsymbol\beta:=u_{\mathrm{vec}}/u^0$ satisfies $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$; the map $\widehat R:=B(\boldsymbol\beta)L$ satisfies $\widehat Re_0=e_0$, $\widehat R(S)=S$ and $\widehat R|_S$ is a spatial rotation of the frame, so that $L=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$; the factorization with a spatial rotation $\widehat R$ and a parameter in the open unit ball is unique; and $L$ is a passive boost if and only if $\widehat R$ is the identity ([[lem-boost-rotation-factorization]]).

[L4] A spatial rotation of the frame is an extension of a linear map $R$ with $Re_0=e_0$, $R(S)\subseteq S$, $\delta(Rw,Rz)=\delta(w,z)$ on $S$ and $\det(R|_S)=+1$; via the $\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ these are exactly the maps whose spatial matrix $A$ satisfies $A^{T}A=I_3$ and $\det A=+1$ ([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]).

[L5] In the frame, $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$, $e_0\in C^+$, and the ordered basis is positively oriented; $\eta(x^0e_0+x^1e_1+x^2e_2+x^3e_3,x^0e_0+x^1e_1+x^2e_2+x^3e_3)=-(x^0)^2+(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[L7] Composition of proper orthochronous Lorentz maps is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map, and every Lorentz map satisfies $\eta(Lv,Lw)=\eta(v,w)$ and $\det L=\pm1$ ([[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]]).

facts: [L1] A $\mathcal C^k$ vector field on $\Omega$ is a map assigning to each point a vector, with components in the inertial chart; for a constant field all partial derivatives of the components vanish, and for a $\mathcal C^1$ vector field $J$ in an inertial chart the continuity equation $\partial_aJ^a=0$ is equivalent to $\partial_0J^0+\sum_i\partial_iJ^i=0$; under the passive boost with parameter $\boldsymbol\beta$, $\Lambda=B(\boldsymbol\beta)$, the components transform as $J'^0=\gamma(J^0-\boldsymbol\beta\cdot J_{\mathrm{cov}})$ and $J'_{\mathrm{cov}}=J_{\mathrm{cov}}+\frac{\gamma-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^2}(\boldsymbol\beta\cdot J_{\mathrm{cov}})\boldsymbol\beta-\gamma\boldsymbol\beta J^0$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]).

[L2] For a $\mathcal C^1$ future timelike vector field $U$ and a $\mathcal C^1$ scalar field $\rho_0$, $J=\rho_0U$ is a $\mathcal C^1$ vector field with first component $J^0=\rho_0U^0$; the normalized chart direction $u:=U/U^0$ satisfies $u^0=1$ and $\rho:=J^0=\rho_0U^0$ is the coordinate density, while $\rho_0$ is the scalar multiplier; $\rho=\rho_0$ holds exactly when $\rho_0(U^0-1)=0$, hence at points with $\rho_0\neq0$ exactly when $U^0=1$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]).

[L3] For $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ the boost acts by $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$ on the $(e_0,e_1)$ plane with $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, and $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[L4] In the frame, $e_0\in C^+$ and the coordinates identify the timelike sets: $T_+=\{v:v^0>|v_{\mathrm{vec}}|\}$, $T_-=\{v:v^0<-|v_{\mathrm{vec}}|\}$, with $C^+=T_+$; a nonzero vector with $\eta(v,v)<0$ is timelike, and $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]).
inverse_uses: [L3] For $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ the boost acts by $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$ on the $(e_0,e_1)$ plane with $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, and $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

chart the four-velocity is $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$ with
$\gamma_w=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and the frame components are read in
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

the spatial part of a frame vector lies in $S=e_0^\perp$ with

$w^1=3c/5$, $w^2=w^3=0$.

$E_n(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $q_n(P)=\sum_im\gamma_ww^ie_i$ for $P=mU$.

$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ for $P=mU$ with $m>0$ and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$.

([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, $m>0$, and let
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) in which a massive particle has
four-velocity $U=\gamma_w(c,w)$
([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(e)) with
$w=(3c/5,0,0)$, so that $\gamma_w=5/4$. Then its four-momentum is $P=mU$ with
components $(5mc/4,\,3mc/4,\,0,\,0)$. Relative to the stationary observer

kinetic energy is $T_n(P)=mc^2/4$, and the mass shell

$25m^2c^4/16-9m^2c^4/16=m^2c^4$. The exact kinetic energy
$mc^2/4=0.25\,mc^2$ exceeds the Newtonian expression
$\tfrac12m|w|^2=9mc^2/50=0.18\,mc^2$; the comparison is a numerical
specialisation, not a limiting claim and not a measurement.

[F4] ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]], clauses (a) and (c)): in an

$(E_{e_0}(P)/c,q^1,q^2,q^3)$, and the combination

[F5] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement (b)): for
$P=mU$ with $m>0$, $U$ future timelike with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and $n$ future

[L1] Chart and spatial structure ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]): in the chart $\eta_0 = \operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the spatial part carries the Euclidean norm $|\cdot|$ and inner product $w \cdot z$.

[L2] Curves ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]): $x$ is $C^{1}$ with tangent $x' = (c,w)$ and is a future timelike worldline exactly when $\eta(x',x') < 0$ with $x'$ future.

[L4] Coordinate form of the decomposition ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]], clause (e)): for a $C^{2}$ future timelike worldline with coordinates $t \mapsto (ct,r(t))$, $w = r'$, $a = w'$, one has $|w| < c$, $U = \gamma_w(c,w)$ with $\gamma_w = (1-|w|^{2}/c^{2})^{-1/2}$, $A^{0} = \gamma_w^{4}(w \cdot a)/c$, $A_{\mathrm{vec}} = \gamma_w^{2}a+\gamma_w^{4}(w \cdot a)w/c^{2}$, and $\eta(A,A) = \gamma_w^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_w^{6}(w \cdot a)^{2}/c^{2}$, vanishing exactly when $a = 0$.

[L2] Ring cylinder data: the material point at chart angle $\phi(t)=\phi_0+\Omega t$ and radius $R$ has coordinates $(ct,R\cos\phi,R\sin\phi,x^3_0)$, and the induced metric on the cylinder is $-(c^2-\Omega^2R^2)dt^2+2\Omega R^2dtd\varphi+R^2d\varphi^2$ with $\varphi=\phi-\Omega t$ ([[pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay]] (i),(iv), [[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (c), [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[L1] The transition is $x'^0=\gamma\bigl(x^0-\tfrac35x^1\bigr)$, $x'^1=\gamma\bigl(x^1-\tfrac35x^0\bigr)$, $x'^2=x^2$, $x'^3=x^3$ with $\gamma=5/4$ ([[lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas]], [[def-lorentz-boost]]).

facts: [L1] If a covector has frame components $(-\varpi,\varpi s_1,\varpi s_2,\varpi s_3)$ with $\varpi>0$ and $|s|=1$, then it is a future null wave covector; its raised vector is $k^\sharp=\varpi(e_0+s_1e_1+s_2e_2+s_3e_3)$ with $k(k^\sharp)=\eta(k^\sharp,k^\sharp)=0$ ([[lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data]], clauses (d) and (e), [[lem-sr-metric-duality-on-lorentz-vector-space]]).

[L2] For inertial charts with $x'=B(\beta)x+b$, $|\beta|<1$, and a future null wave covector with frame-$x$ data $(\varpi,s)$, the frame-$x'$ data satisfies $\varpi'=\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\varpi$, $s'_i=\bigl[s_i+\frac{\gamma-1}{|\beta|^2}(\beta\cdot s)\beta_i-\gamma\beta_i\bigr]/\bigl[\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\bigr]$ for $\beta\ne0$, and in the axis case $\beta=be_1$: $s'_1=(s_1-b)/(1-bs_1)$, $s'_2=s_2/[\gamma(1-bs_1)]$, $s'_3=s_3/[\gamma(1-bs_1)]$; applying the transformation with $-\beta$ returns the original data ([[lem-sr-null-covector-boost-transformation]], clauses (ii), (iii), (v)).

[L3] $B(\beta)$ is the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] with $\gamma=(1-|\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$, and $B(\beta)$ is proper orthochronous with $B(-\beta)=B(\beta)^{-1}$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]); the frame is an inertial frame with an inertial chart ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[L2] Coordinate criterion and sums: $q\in I^+(p)$ iff $D^0>|D_s|$ for $D=x(q)-x(p)$, and the sum of finitely many future causal vectors is future causal, strictly timelike if one summand is future timelike; the sum of two nonparallel future null vectors is future causal but not null, hence future timelike ([[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]]).

[L3] Straight paths and reachability: the straight path $s\mapsto p+s(q-p)$ has constant tangent $q-p$, and for $q\ne p$ one has $q\in J^+(p)$ iff that straight path is a future causal path, with $I^+(p)$ characterized by the straight path being future timelike ([[thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence]], [[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]]).

[L4] Piecewise $C^1$ curves: the concatenation of the two straight legs is a piecewise $C^1$ curve with constant tangents $(1,1,0,0)$ and $(1,0,1,0)$ on the open pieces and one-sided difference-quotient tangents equal to those vectors at every point of $[0,2]$ ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]).

facts:
[F1] ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] and
[[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]): the frame basis is $\eta$-orthonormal with
$\eta(e_0,e_0)=-1$, $\eta(e_1,e_1)=1$, $\eta(e_0,e_1)=0$; $\eta$ is bilinear,
so $\eta(P_1,P_2)=(E_1E_2/c^2)\bigl(\eta(e_0,e_0)-\eta(e_1,e_1)\bigr)$ and
components add.

[F4] ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], Definition):
$E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$ for $P\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ and future unit $n$.

[F5] ([[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]], Definition): the
total of a finite list is the finite sum; the invariant mass of a future
timelike total is $M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$; for a future null total $M=0$ by
convention.

[F6] ([[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]], Statement (a)–(c)): a future
timelike $Q$ with invariant mass $M$ has an inertial frame with
$e_0=Q/(Mc)$ and $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$; if an inertial frame satisfies
$q_{e_0}(Q)=0$ then $e_0=Q/(Mc)$; a nonzero future null vector has no
center-of-momentum frame.

[F7] ([[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]], Statement (d)): for future
null $P_i=(E_i/c)(e_0+s_i)$ with unit $s_i$ and $\sigma=s_1\cdot s_2$, the
total is future timelike for $\sigma<1$ with
$M=\sqrt{2E_1E_2(1-\sigma)}/c^2$, and for $\sigma=1$ ($\theta=0$, parallel
spatial directions) it is future null with $M=0$ and no center-of-momentum
frame.

[L2] Chart ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]): the chart's observer is $e_0$, and $n^{\perp} = \operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is the Euclidean spatial space of the frame with $|w| = \sqrt{\delta(w,w)}$.
[L4] Observer clause ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]): the four-velocity of the observer's own worldline with future unit timelike $n$ is $cn$.

[L1] For $|\beta|<1$ the passive boost in the $1+1$ case $\boldsymbol\beta=\beta e_1$ acts on the coordinates of the $(e_0,e_1)$ plane by $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$, with $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}>0$ and $\gamma$ the rational power of the positive base $1-\beta^2$; the matrix in the ordered basis $(e_0,e_1)$ is $\begin{pmatrix}\gamma&-\gamma\beta\\ -\gamma\beta&\gamma\end{pmatrix}$, and the map fixes every vector with vanishing coordinates in the $e_1$ direction ([[def-lorentz-boost]]).

[L2] $B(\beta)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with $B(\beta)^{-1}=B(-\beta)$, and $B(\beta)e_0=\gamma(e_0-\beta e_1)$; the map $\beta\mapsto B(\beta)$ is injective ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[L3] In an inertial frame $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ and $e_0\in C^+$; one has $\eta(x^0e_0+x^1e_1,x^0e_0+x^1e_1)=-(x^0)^2+(x^1)^2$ in the plane coordinates ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[L4] $C^+$ is one of the two components of the timelike set and is the set of future timelike vectors; a Lorentz map is orthochronous exactly when it maps $C^+$ onto $C^+$ ([[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[F1] The experimental-interface vocabulary: an operational model is a tuple $M=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ with $S$ nonempty, $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ nonempty, $\theta:S\to\Theta$ surjective, $D$ assigning run descriptions and $F:\Theta\to\mathbb R^d$ a prediction map whose components are required, by the declared interpretation $(*)$, to be numbers the framework assigns to $D(s)$ with every intermediate quantity, frame, event, sign and unit declared; a data record $R=(N,z,\varepsilon,a)$ declares that each value lies in the closed box $\prod_j[z_{k,j}-\varepsilon_{k,j},z_{k,j}+\varepsilon_{k,j}]$ in the declared units ([[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]]).

[F2] Doppler theorem clauses (i) and (ii): for inertial charts whose transition is $x'=B(\beta)x+b$ with $\beta\in\mathbb R^3$, $|\beta|<1$, the same future null wave covector $k$ with frame-$x$ data $(\omega,s)$ has frame-$x'$ data $(\omega',s')$ with $\omega'=\gamma(1-\beta\cdot s)\omega$, where $\gamma=(1-|\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$; and the rest observers of $x$ and $x'$, of four-velocities $c e_0$ and $c e'_0$, read the angular frequencies $\omega=-c k(e_0)$ and $\omega'=-c k(e'_0)$ ([[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]]).

[F3] Observer angular frequency and wave data: the observer of four-velocity $U_o=c n$, with $\eta(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ future, reads $\omega_n:=-c k(n)=-k(U_o)$ in the SI convention $x^0=ct$; a future null wave covector has frame components $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ with $\omega>0$ and $|s|=1$ ([[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]]).

[F4] Frame-data lemma clauses (a),(b),(e): for a future null wave covector in a frame, $\varpi:=-k(e_0)>0$ and $|s|=1$; conversely, a covector whose frame components are $(-\varpi,\varpi s_1,\varpi s_2,\varpi s_3)$ with $\varpi>0$ and $|s|=1$ is a future null wave covector ([[lem-sr-null-covector-frame-data]]).

[F5] Passive boost: for $\beta$ with $|\beta|<1$ the map $B(\beta)$ is defined in an inertial frame's coordinates by $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta\cdot x)$ and $x'=x+((\gamma-1)/|\beta|^2)(\beta\cdot x)\beta-\gamma\beta x^0$ for $\beta\neq0$, with $B(0)$ the identity, so that in the axis case $\beta=\beta e_1$ one has $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]]); it is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map, $B(\beta)^{-1}=B(-\beta)$, and $B(\beta)e_0=\gamma(e_0-\beta_1 e_1-\beta_2 e_2-\beta_3 e_3)$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[F6] Inertial frame and chart: an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ consists of an event $o\in A$ and an ordered basis of $V$ that is $\eta$-orthonormal, future and positively oriented; its chart is $x(p)=E^{-1}(p-o)$ with $E(u)=\sum_a u^a e_a$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

[A1] Adopted ideal plane-wave model: an ideal monochromatic light wave in vacuum is modeled in any inertial chart by a dimensionless affine phase with future null wave covector, and an ideal observer of four-velocity $U_o=c n$ receiving this wave reads the frequency $\omega_n=-c k(n)$ ([[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]]).

[F7] SI conventions: in every inertial chart $x^0=ct$ with $c>0$ in metres per second, spatial coordinates in metres, and the matrix of $\eta$ equal to $\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]).

future timelike $P$ the invariant mass is

an inertial frame with $q_{e_0}(P)=0$, equivalently
$P\in\mathrm{span}(e_0)$, and the condition is equivalent to
$P=-\eta(P,e_0)e_0$.

[F2] ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]], Definition):
$E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$ and $q_n(P)=h(P)=P+\eta(P,n)n\in n^\perp$ for
$P\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ and future unit $n$.

[F3] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement (a)): if $P$
is nonzero future causal and $n$ future unit, then $E_n(P)>0$; if $P$ is
future timelike with invariant mass $m(P)$, then
$m(P)^2=-\eta(P,P)/c^2$.

[F4] ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]], clause (c)): for
future unit $n$, the map $h$ is linear with image $n^\perp$ and kernel
$\mathrm{span}(n)$, $V=\mathrm{span}(n)\oplus n^\perp$, and the restriction of
$\eta$ to $n^\perp$ is positive definite; hence $\eta$ restricted to
$n^\perp$ is an inner product.

[F6] ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], Definition): an inertial
frame is a tuple $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $o\in A$ and $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$
an $\eta$-orthonormal ordered basis of $V$ that is future and positively
oriented; its inertial chart sends $p$ to the coordinates relative to
$(o;e_0,\dots,e_3)$.

[F7] ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]], Definition): the oriented volume
form $\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)$ is the determinant of the coordinate matrix in
an inertial frame, an alternating $4$-linear form; replacing one basis vector
by its negative changes the determinant's sign.

[F8] ([[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]], Statement): in every
oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space and for every event $o$ there
exists an inertial frame with origin $o$; explicitly, from an
$\eta$-orthonormal basis an orientation may be corrected by negating one
spatial vector without destroying $\eta$-orthonormality or the future first
vector.

facts: [L1] Causal signal restriction: a signal is information or a physical marker correlating a prepared operation at the emission event with an observation at the reception event within the model, and the model admits a transmission carrying a signal from $p$ to $q$ only if $q\in J^+(p)$, that is only if $q-p$ is zero or future causal; ideal vacuum light signals are the future null boundary case; the restriction is adopted, not derived, and not an empirical claim; kinematic patterns from independent prearranged mechanisms are explicitly not restricted ([[post-sr-causal-signal-propagation]]).

[L2] Criterion and cone description: $\overline{C^+}$ is a convex cone with $\overline{C^+}\cap\overline{C^-}=\{0\}$; for $D=x(q)-x(p)$, $q\in J^+(p)$ iff $D^0\ge|D_s|$; $q\in I^+(p)$ iff $D^0>|D_s|$; every nonzero element of $\overline{C^+}$ has $D^0>0$; sums of finitely many elements of $\overline{C^+}$ lie in $\overline{C^+}$, and if one summand lies in $C^+$ the sum lies in $C^+$ ([[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]]).

[L3] Spacelike pairs: for $q-p$ spacelike one has $|D^0|<|D_s|$ in every inertial chart, and there are inertial frames whose charts give $x^0(q)-x^0(p)$ either sign and inertial frames of simultaneity ([[lem-sr-spacelike-pairs-have-frame-dependent-time-order]]).

[L4] Causal loops and covariance: if $p\le q$ and $q\le p$ then $p=q$; and for every proper orthochronous affine Lorentz map $F$ one has $F(J^+(p))=J^+(F(p))$, $F(I^+(p))=I^+(F(p))$, and $p\le q$ iff $F(p)\le F(q)$ ([[thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence]]).

[L5] Inertial covariance: the equations of the specified model are covariant under the affine maps with proper orthochronous Lorentz linear part, and those maps are the inertial changes of description ([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]).

[L6] Interval and cone invariance: the causal classification of a displacement and, for causal displacements, the future/past alternative are independent of the inertial chart, and the interval computed from coordinates is chart independent ([[pthm-sr-interval-and-cone-invariance]], [[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]], [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]).

facts:
[F1] ([[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], Postulate (i) and (ii)): every
massive classical particle carries a positive constant mass parameter $m>0$
and has four-momentum $P=mU$; relative to a future unit observer $n$ the model
identifies the measured energy with $E_n(P)$, the measured spatial momentum
with $q_n(P)$, the kinetic energy with $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and the rest
energy with $mc^2$; the SI unit of $P$ is kilogram metre per second.

[F2] ([[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]], Postulate (i) and (ii)):
an ideal massless particle is described by a nonzero future null vector $P$,
with measured energy and spatial momentum identified with $E_n(P)$ and
$q_n(P)$; it is not of the form $mU$ for any $m>0$ and future timelike $U$
with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and it has no four-velocity, no proper-time
parametrisation and no rest frame.

[F3] ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]], Statement (a) and (b)):
for nonzero future causal $P$ and future unit $n$, $E_n(P)>0$ and the mass
shell and null identities hold; for $P=mU$ with $m>0$, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and
$\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$, one has $E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma$,
$T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)\ge0$, $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if $U=cn$, and
$m(P)=m$.

[F4] ([[lem-sr-four-momentum-in-inertial-frame]], Statement (a)–(c)): in an
inertial frame with $n=e_0$ the components are
$(P^0,P^1,P^2,P^3)=(E_n(P)/c,q^1,q^2,q^3)$ and the mass-shell identity holds
in components; for $P=mU$ with chart coordinate velocity $w$ one has
$E=m\gamma_wc^2$, $\mathbf p=m\gamma_w\mathbf w$; under a passive boost the
components transform as the components of $P$, the combination
$E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2$ is invariant and equals $m(P)^2c^4$ for future timelike
$P$ and $0$ for future null $P$.

[F5] ([[lem-sr-four-force-and-work-energy-identities]], Statement (a)–(d)):
with $F=\dot P$ the four-force of
[[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]] along a $C^2$ worldline,
$F=mA$, $\eta(P,F)=0$, $F=\gamma(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\mathbf f)$,
$dE/dt=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$ for constant $m$, and
$\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,dm/d\tau$ for a $C^1$ variable mass parameter.

[F6] ([[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]], Definition): side
totals are finite sums; the invariant mass of a future timelike total $Q$ is
$M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$; for a future null total $M=0$ by convention; a
center-of-momentum frame of a nonzero total is an inertial frame with
$q_{e_0}(Q)=0$.

[F7] ([[lem-sr-finite-future-causal-sums]], Statement): for nonzero future
causal $P_1,\dots,P_N$, the total $Q=\sum_iP_i$ is nonzero future causal and
is future timelike if some $P_i$ is future timelike; $-\eta(v,w)\ge0$ for
$v,w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ with equality if and only if $v=0$, or $w=0$, or both
are nonzero future null with $w=\lambda v$, $\lambda>0$; $E_n$ and $q_n$ are
additive over finite sums, with $E_n(Q)>0$.

[F8] ([[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]], Statement (a) and (c)): for future
timelike $Q$ with invariant mass $M$ there is an inertial frame with
$e_0=Q/(Mc)$, $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$ and $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$; a nonzero future null
vector has no center-of-momentum frame.

[F9] ([[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]], Definition): a collision
datum consists of an event and two finite nonempty lists of legs with side
totals; it conserves when the totals are equal; a mass-specified datum is
on-shell with recorded masses; a causal datum has all legs in
$\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$.

[F10] ([[lem-sr-collision-necessary-conditions]], Statement (a), (c) and
(d)): for a mass-specified conserving causal on-shell datum with nonzero legs
and future timelike total $Q$ of invariant mass $M$, each side satisfies
$M\ge\sum m_\ell$ over its massive legs with equality exactly when the side is
massive-only and all its massive legs are at rest in the center-of-momentum
frame; for the two-leg incoming side $P_i=m_iU_i$ with $n_2=U_2/c$,
$\gamma=-\eta(U_1/c,n_2)$ and $E=E_{n_2}(P_1)=m_1c^2\gamma$, one has
$M^2=m_1^2+m_2^2+2m_2E/c^2$, giving the stated thresholds for an outgoing
massive-mass sum $\sum_j\mu_j$; and a conserving datum with a single null
incoming leg and an outgoing massive leg does not exist.

[F11] ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], Definition): in the
framework's conventions the four-momentum has the unit kilogram metre per
second and the observer energy the unit joule.

[L1] The adopted postulate: $P=mU$ with constant $m>0$ and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ (clause (i)); the model identifies the measured energy, spatial momentum, kinetic energy and rest energy of the particle with $E_n(P)$, $q_n(P)$, $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and $mc^2$ (clause (ii)); units as in [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] ([[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]).

[A2] Ideal clock reading rule ([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] (i)): along a curve whose coordinate representation in an inertial chart is $C^1$ with everywhere future timelike derivative, an ideal clock reads between parameters $a<b$ the value $c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}\,\mathrm ds$, with no additional acceleration-dependent term.

[A3] Clock hypothesis for the general worldline class ([[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] (ii)): an ideal clock carried along a future timelike worldline of the model, including an accelerated one and a weak piecewise $C^1$ one with finitely many kinks, reads between two parameter values the proper-time difference $\Delta\tau$ of [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]] (for weak piecewise $C^1$ histories), with no term depending on acceleration, jerk or any higher derivative; the reading does not depend on an increasing regular change of parameter.

[L4] Endpoint bound and flat maximum ([[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]]): for the weak piecewise future timelike $x$ from $p$ to $q$, $c\Delta\tau(x)\le T$; equality holds exactly for the strictly increasing reparametrizations of the straight segment in the sense of that theorem's clause (ii); and if the image of $x$ is not contained in the straight segment, in particular if $x$ is piecewise inertial with piece tangents not all positive multiples of one another, then $c\Delta\tau(x)<T$, while a piecewise inertial itinerary whose tangents are all positive multiples of one another attains the bound.

[L5] Proper-time definition and chart independence ([[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]], [[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]): $\Delta\tau(x)=c^{-1}\sum_i\int_{(s_{i-1},s_i)}\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ is defined through the intrinsic integrand $\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$, is independent of the inertial chart and of the admissible partition, and for the straight worldline with constant tangent $d/(b-a)$ equals $c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(d,d)}$, the straight-segment value of [[def-sr-proper-time]].

[L7] Piecewise inertial histories ([[def-sr-inertial-and-piecewise-inertial-worldline]]): a piecewise inertial worldline is a weak piecewise $C^1$ future timelike worldline with constant future timelike tangents on the open pieces.

direct_context:
**Derived (constructed, not adopted) on this page.** Displacements and
intervals; the causal classification of displacements; inertial frames and
their inertial charts ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]); the smooth
structure of $A$ making it a smooth $4$-manifold and the canonical identification
$T_pA\cong V$; the oriented volume form and its components
([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]); and the spatial Euclidean structure
and vector product of a named inertial frame
([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]). These are
mathematical constructions from the primitive structure, with the stated
frame-dependence where it occurs.

This framework adopts the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), its inertial frames and inertial charts
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), and the assertion that inertial
changes of description are governed by that geometry
([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]). The transformation law derived on this page
is a conditional consequence of that adoption. This remark records the
epistemic status of the starting point; it makes no further physical or
mathematical claim.

facts: [L1] The framework adopts the affine Minkowski model as spacetime with its causal structure ([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

[L2] In every inertial chart $x^0=ct$, the matrix of $\eta$ is $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ in the orthonormal frame, and points are determined by their coordinates ([[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).
[L3] A curve is $C^k$ exactly when its coordinate representation is; its tangent is read in $V$; a $C^2$ curve has $C^1$-in-parameter tangents ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] (a)).

[L4] Causal classification and the chart criterion: timelike means $\eta(v,v)<0$ and $C^+=\{v:v^0>|v_s|\}$ in every inertial chart ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]] (a)).

[L5] Four-velocity of a $C^1$ future timelike worldline: $U=x'/\tau'=cx'/\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$, with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$; for $C^2$ curves the four-acceleration is the proper-time derivative of $U$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] (a),(b), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a)).
[L6] Proper time $\tau(t)=\int_0^t c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}\,dv$ up to a constant, and the reparametrization tangent $x'/\tau'$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]).

[L7] The Lorentz factor of the future unit field $n=\gamma(1,\beta,0,0)$ relative to the inertial chart observer $e_0$ is $\gamma\ge1$ with $\gamma=1$ iff $\beta=0$; along a congruence flow line the four-velocity is $cn$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (d), (a)).

[L8] Material metric and its evolution: for a $C^2$ injective immersion $\Phi$ with material directions $e_I=\partial_{\xi^I}\Phi$, $G_{IJ}=h(e_I,e_J)$ is a $C^1$ positive-definite material metric; $\partial_\tau G_{IJ}=2c\theta(e_I,e_J)$; for nonzero $e_I$, $\ell_I=\sqrt{G_{II}}$ satisfies $\partial_\tau\ell_I=c\theta(u_I,u_I)\ell_I$ with $u_I=h(e_I)/\ell_I$; $\theta=0$ makes $G$ constant in the flow parameter; horizontality of $\theta$ gives $\theta(e_I/\ell_I,e_I/\ell_I)=\theta(u_I,u_I)$ ([[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]] (a)-(d)).

[L9] Born rigidity and expansion: for $C^1$ data the projected deformation $\theta_{ab}=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\partial_{(c}n_{d)}$ kills $n$-components, and Born rigidity $\theta=0$ agrees with the smooth definition; restriction to a subfamily keeps the induced metric data ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (c),(d), [[lem-sr-connecting-field-stretching]]).

[L10] Translated-congruence data: for the $C^1$ field $n=\gamma(1,\beta,0,0)$ of the translated worldlines the unit longitudinal rest vector is $s=\gamma(\beta,1,0,0)$ and $\theta(s,s)=\gamma^3q'q''/c^3$, nonzero exactly where $q'q''\ne0$; and the Rindler congruence is Born rigid with constant rest slices and accelerations $\rho^{-1}\partial_\rho$, $\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})=\rho^{-2}$ ([[thm-sr-fermi-walker-and-rigid-observer-examples]] (b),(d)).

[L11] Proper acceleration of a congruence flow line: $a=c^2\sqrt{\eta(a_{\mathrm{cg}},a_{\mathrm{cg}})}$, so $\rho$-const Rindler flow lines have proper acceleration $c^2/\rho$ ([[def-sr-proper-acceleration]] (b)).

[L12] The covariant derivative of a $C^1$ field along a curve is the ordinary derivative of its components; for $C^1$ data the first-order coordinate formulas of [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] (d),(e) apply.
direct_context: Adopt [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and the SI conventions $x^0=ct$ of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] in an inertial chart ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Let $J$ be an open interval containing $0$, let $q:J\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ with $|q'(t)|<c$, set $\beta=q'/c$ and $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, let $L>0$, and fix transverse coordinates $(y_0,z_0)$. The rocket and thread-element worldlines are $x_\xi(t)=x^{-1}(ct,q(t)+\xi,y_0,z_0)$, with labels in an open interval $I$ containing $[0,L]$; the rockets are labels $0,L$.

facts: [A1] Inertial covariance ([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]): the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space is the spacetime of the framework, and the model's equations are covariant under the affine maps preserving $\eta$, orientation and the future cone.

[A2] Ideal-clock reading rule ([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] (i)): along a $C^1$ history with everywhere future timelike derivative the ideal clock reads, between parameters $a<b$, the value $c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}\,\mathrm ds$, with no acceleration-dependent term.

[A3] Clock hypothesis for the piecewise class ([[post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis]] (ii)): an ideal clock carried along a future timelike worldline of the model, including a weak piecewise $C^1$ one with finitely many kinks, reads the proper-time difference $\Delta\tau$ of [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]], with no term depending on acceleration, jerk or higher derivatives.

[L4] Inertial and piecewise inertial worldlines ([[def-sr-inertial-and-piecewise-inertial-worldline]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]): a curve with constant tangent $d$ along an interval is inertial when $d$ is future timelike; a two-piece curve with constant future timelike tangents $d_1,d_2$ joining at a corner is a piecewise inertial weak piecewise $C^1$ future timelike worldline; and in the chart a coordinate vector $(w^0,w_s)$ is future timelike exactly when $w^0>|w_s|$.

[L5] Proper times of straight and piecewise straight histories ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]): a straight history with constant tangent $w$ over a parameter interval of length $L$ has proper time $c^{-1}L\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}$; a two-leg history has total proper time the sum of its leg values; and the values depend only on the intrinsic integrand $\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ and the parameter interval, not on the inertial chart.

[L6] Same-endpoint clock comparison ([[pthm-sr-same-endpoint-clock-comparison]]): for a weak piecewise future timelike history from $p$ to $q$ with $q-p$ future timelike, the clock reading along the straight history is $c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}$ and is the largest among the readings of the class, with strict inequality for every history whose image is not the straight segment; the conclusion is conditional on the same postulates.

[L7] Endpoint theorem ([[thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum]]): for the weak piecewise future timelike class, $c\,\Delta\tau\le\sqrt{-\eta(q-p,q-p)}$ with the stated equality and strictness clauses.

[L1] Coordinate criterion, cone description and sums: for $D=x(q)-x(p)$, $q\in J^+(p)$ iff $D^0\ge|D_s|$, $q\in I^+(p)$ iff $D^0>|D_s|$, and the past statements hold with $-D$; nonzero elements of $\overline{C^+}$ have positive time coordinate; $\overline{C^+}\cap\overline{C^-}=\{0\}$; sums of finitely many elements of $\overline{C^+}$ lie in $\overline{C^+}$, strictly in $C^+$ if one summand lies in $C^+$ ([[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]], [[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

[L4] Signals: the model admits a transmission carrying a signal from $p$ to $q$ only if $q\in J^+(p)$; relaying two transmissions $p\to q$ and $q\to r$ gives $r\in J^+(p)$, strictly $r\in I^+(p)$ if one leg is strict, and two transmissions $p\to q$ and $q\to p$ force $p=q$ ([[post-sr-causal-signal-propagation]], [[pthm-sr-causal-signal-order-and-composition]]).

[L5] Boosts: for $|\beta|<1$ the passive boost acts by $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$ in the $(0,1)$-plane and is proper orthochronous with inverse $B(\beta)^{-1}=B(-\beta)$; the inverse transformation reads $x^0=\gamma(x'^0+\beta x'^1)$, $x^1=\gamma(x'^1+\beta x'^0)$; the chart $x'=B(\beta)\circ x$ is the chart of an inertial frame ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]], [[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]).

[L6] Invariance: the interval $\eta(D,D)$, the causal character of a displacement and, for causal displacements, the future/past alternative are independent of the inertial chart; every proper orthochronous Lorentz map preserves $\eta$, the causal character and the closed cones ([[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]], [[pthm-sr-interval-and-cone-invariance]], [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]).

[L7] Frame-dependent order of spacelike pairs: for a spacelike displacement there are inertial charts assigning the time-coordinate difference either sign and inertial charts of simultaneity ([[lem-sr-spacelike-pairs-have-frame-dependent-time-order]]).
inverse_uses: [L5] Boosts: for $|\beta|<1$ the passive boost acts by $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$ in the $(0,1)$-plane and is proper orthochronous with inverse $B(\beta)^{-1}=B(-\beta)$; the inverse transformation reads $x^0=\gamma(x'^0+\beta x'^1)$, $x^1=\gamma(x'^1+\beta x'^0)$; the chart $x'=B(\beta)\circ x$ is the chart of an inertial frame ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]], [[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]).

facts: [L1] A linear map $L:V\to V$ with $\eta(Lv,Lw)=\eta(v,w)$ for all $v,w$ is a linear Lorentz map; an affine Lorentz map is a map $F:A\to A$ with $F(p)=F(p_0)+L(p-p_0)$ for a linear Lorentz map $L$, and its linear part $L$ is unique ([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]).
[L2] Affine Lorentz maps are bijections and form a group under composition ([[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]]).

[L4] For the inertial chart $x$, $x(p)=E^{-1}(p-o)$; $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$, so $\eta(Ea,Eb)=\eta_0(a,b)$ with $\eta_0=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; the chart is a bijection $A\to\mathbb R^4$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).
[L5] The inertial charts form a smooth atlas; the transitions between inertial charts are affine, hence smooth ([[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]]).

[L6] The tangent space at every event is canonically identified with $V$; for an inertial chart the identification is $\Phi_p(v)=\sum_av^a\partial_a|_p$ for $v=\sum_av^ae_a$, and under this identification the total derivative of a chart-represented map is the coordinate total derivative conjugated by $E$ ([[lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v]]).

[F1] Endpoint displacement ([[lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline]]): $d=q-p$ is future timelike, so $T>0$, and in every inertial chart the time component of $d$ is positive and dominates the norm of its spatial part.

[F2] Rest frame of the displacement ([[lem-sr-rest-frame-of-a-future-timelike-displacement]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]): $n:=d/T$ is future unit timelike, for every event $o$ there is an inertial frame with first vector $n$, and for the chart $\xi$ of any such frame $\xi(o+\lambda d)=(\lambda T,0,0,0)$ for every real $\lambda$; in particular with $o:=p$ one has $\xi(p)=(0,0,0,0)$ and $\xi(q)=(T,0,0,0)$.

[F3] Weak piecewise structure and proper time ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], [[lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability]], [[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]], [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[def-oriented-integral]]): $x$ is $C^1$ on each open piece with future timelike interior tangent and has finite one-sided difference-quotient tangents; on a piece $(\alpha,\beta)$ with coordinate path $y=(y^0,z)$ one has $y^0{}'>|z'|\ge0$, the density $g=\sqrt{(y^0{}')^2-|z'|^2}=\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ has a finite positive improper integral $\int_{(\alpha,\beta)}g$ in the two-sided convention, the signed improper integral of $y^0{}'$ over the piece equals $y^0(\beta)-y^0(\alpha)$, improper values are additive under subdivision, and the finite piece sums are independent of the admissible partition; $\Delta\tau(x)=c^{-1}\sum_i\int_{(s_{i-1},s_i)}g$, the based proper-time function is strictly increasing, and under the corner hypothesis (H) the improper values coincide with the ordinary Riemann integrals, agreeing with [[def-sr-proper-time]] in the globally $C^1$ case.

[F4] Cone coordinates and metric ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]): in an inertial chart a vector with coordinates $(v^0,v_s)$ is future timelike exactly when $v^0>|v_s|$, and $-\eta(v,v)=(v^0)^2-|v_s|^2$; a constant-tangent worldline on $[a,b]$ with tangent the future timelike $w$ has total proper time $c^{-1}(b-a)\sqrt{-\eta(w,w)}$.

[F1] Fermi–Walker derivative: $D_{\mathrm{FW}}X/d\tau=X'/\tau'-c^{-2}\bigl(\eta(A,X)U-\eta(U,X)A\bigr)$; the four-velocity satisfies $D_{\mathrm{FW}}U/d\tau=0$; where primes refer to the generic curve parameter $s$ and $\tau'>0$; existence and uniqueness of transported fields with prescribed initial values hold, and the solution map is linear ([[def-sr-fermi-walker-transport]] clauses (a),(b), [[lem-sr-fermi-walker-transport-existence-and-uniqueness]]).

[F2] In an inertial chart, $\eta(u,v)=-u^0v^0+u^1v^1+u^2v^2+u^3v^3$, the flat covariant derivative acts on components by ordinary coordinate derivatives $\partial_a$, is torsion-free and metric compatible, and its first-order $C^1$ version is available: for $C^1$ fields $(\nabla_XY)^a=X^b\partial_bY^a$ and $[X,Y]^a=X^b\partial_bY^a-Y^b\partial_bX^a$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

[F3] Kinematics: $\nabla_an_b=-n_aa_b+\theta_{ab}+\omega_{ab}$, $\theta$ symmetric, $\omega$ antisymmetric, both horizontal, $(\mathcal L_nh)_{ab}=2\theta_{ab}$, so Born rigidity is $\theta=0$; for the metric dual $\alpha=n^\flat$, $\alpha\wedge d\alpha=0$ on an open set if and only if $\omega=0$ there, if and only if the rest distribution $\ker\alpha$ is integrable there ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]]).

[F6] Lie bracket: $[X,Y]^a=X^b\partial_bY^a-Y^b\partial_bX^a$ and $[fX,Y]=f[X,Y]-Y(f)X$ for a smooth function $f$ ([[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], [[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]]).

[F7] A tetra d at an event is an ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ and $e_0$ future; a congruence is a smooth field $n$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, $n$ future; a vector with components $(u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3)$ in an inertial frame is future timelike if and only if $-u^0{}^2+|\vec u|^2<0$ and $u^0>0$ ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).
direct_context: **Given:** The affine Minkowski model with its inertial chart calculus, the Fermi–Walker transport rule of [[def-sr-fermi-walker-transport]], the congruence kinematics and Frobenius criterion of [[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] and [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]], and the four explicit data sets (a)–(d) of the Statement ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]).

facts: [L1] Weak piecewise causal integrability: for a piecewise $C^1$ curve with nonzero future causal one-sided tangents and any inertial chart with coordinates $(y^0,z)$, $z\in\mathbb R^3$, one has $y^{0'}\ge|z'|\ge0$ and $y^{0'}>0$ on the open pieces; every coordinate derivative is absolutely improperly Riemann integrable with signed improper integral equal to the corresponding endpoint increment; $f=\sqrt{(y^{0'})^2-|z'|^2}=\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$ has finite nonnegative improper integrals with $\int f\le\int y^{0'}=y^0(\beta)-y^0(\alpha)$ on each piece; the improper values are independent of the intermediate point and additive under subdivision and the finite piece sums are independent of the admissible partition; $D=x(b)-x(a)$ is nonzero future causal with $D^0>0$ and $|D_s|\le D^0$ in every inertial chart; if some interior or one-sided endpoint tangent is future timelike then $D$ is future timelike; coordinate time is strictly increasing on every nondegenerate subinterval; no derivative-limit hypothesis and no choice principle is used ([[lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability]]).

[L2] Total proper time of a piecewise $C^1$ future timelike worldline is $\Delta\tau=c^{-1}\sum_i\int_{(a_i,b_i)}g_i$ with $g_i=\sqrt{-\eta(y',y')}>0$ the improper integrals of [L1]; it is independent of the partition, additive over concatenation, positive, and carries exactly one factor $c^{-1}$; under the corner hypothesis (finite derivative limits) the improper integrals are ordinary Riemann integrals ([[def-sr-piecewise-proper-time]], [[def-sr-proper-time]]).

[L3] Cone description and coordinate criterion: $C^+=\{v:v^0>|v_s|\}$, $\overline{C^+}=\{v:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$, $C^-=\{v:-v^0>|v_s|\}$, $\overline{C^-}=\{v:-v^0\ge|v_s|\}$, every nonzero $v\in\overline{C^+}$ satisfies $v^0>0$, $v$ is future null exactly when $|v_s|=v^0>0$, and $q\in J^+(p)$ iff $D^0\ge|D_s|$, $q\in I^+(p)$ iff $D^0>|D_s|$ for $D=x(q)-x(p)$; the closed cones are convex cones with $\overline{C^+}\cap\overline{C^-}=\{0\}$ and a causal vector is future or past but not both ([[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]), while the two displayed descriptions give $\overline{C^-}=-\overline{C^+}$ ([[lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion]]).

[L4] Reachability: $p\le q$ iff $q-p\in\overline{C^+}$ and $p<q$ iff $q-p\in C^+$; $J^+(p)=p+\overline{C^+}$, $I^+(p)=p+C^+$ and the past versions; a piecewise $C^1$ future causal path is a piecewise $C^1$ curve whose one-sided tangents at every point are future causal; $q$ is reachable from $p$ by a future causal path when $p=q$ or when a piecewise $C^1$ future causal path joins them, and $R^+(p)$ is the set of such $q$ ([[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]]).

[L5] Coordinates: in the ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of an inertial frame one has $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, so for $v=\sum_a v^ae_a$, $w=\sum_a w^ae_a$ one has $\eta(v,w)=-v^0w^0+\delta(v_s,w_s)$ with $v_s= v^1e_1+v^2e_2+v^3e_3$ and the positive-definite restriction $\delta=\eta|_S$; in particular $\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+|v_s|^2$ and $|v_s|^2=\delta(v_s,v_s)=\sum_{i=1}^3(v^i)^2$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

[L6] Curves: differentiability, $C^1$ and piecewise $C^1$ regularity with finite one-sided difference-quotient tangents, and the tangent $x'(s)$ of a curve in $A$; for the straight path $\sigma(s)=p+sD$ one has $\sigma(s+h)-\sigma(s)=hD$, so $\sigma'\equiv D$; a compact interval $[a,b]$ has $a<b$ in the sense of [[def-interval]] ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], [[def-affine-space-and-displacement]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-derivative]]).

[L7] Boosts: for $|\beta|<1$ the passive boost $B(\beta)$ acts in the $(0,1)$-plane by $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$ with $\gamma=(1-|\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$; $B(\beta)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with $B(\beta)^{-1}=B(-\beta)$; if $u$ is future unit timelike with coordinates $(u^0,u_{\mathrm{vec}})$ then $B(\beta)u=e_0$ for $\beta=u_{\mathrm{vec}}/u^0$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[L8] Lorentz maps: an affine Lorentz map has the form $F(r)=F(p_0)+L(r-p_0)$ with $L$ a linear Lorentz map, uniquely determined, satisfying $\eta(Lv,Lw)=\eta(v,w)$; every linear Lorentz map is a bijection, $L(C^+)$ is $C^+$ or $C^-$, and every element of $SO^+(V,\eta)$ preserves $\eta$, the causal character of every nonzero vector, the future and past closed cones, the orientation and the oriented volume form; the composition and inverse of affine Lorentz maps are affine Lorentz maps ([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]], [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]], [[def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map]], [[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]).
inverse_uses: [L7] Boosts: for $|\beta|<1$ the passive boost $B(\beta)$ acts in the $(0,1)$-plane by $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$ with $\gamma=(1-|\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$; $B(\beta)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with $B(\beta)^{-1}=B(-\beta)$; if $u$ is future unit timelike with coordinates $(u^0,u_{\mathrm{vec}})$ then $B(\beta)u=e_0$ for $\beta=u_{\mathrm{vec}}/u^0$ ([[def-lorentz-boost]], [[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

facts: [L1] A linear Lorentz map is a linear $L$ with $\eta(Lv,Lw)=\eta(v,w)$ for all $v,w$; it is proper when $\det L=+1$ and orthochronous when $L(C^+)=C^+$; $GL(V)$ is the group of invertible linear maps ([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]).

[L2] Every linear Lorentz map is a linear isomorphism, satisfies $\det L=\pm1$, preserves $\eta(v,v)$ and the causal character of every nonzero vector, and maps $C^+$ onto one of the two components $C^+,C^-$ of the timelike set; $L(C^+)=C^+$ holds if and only if $L(C^+)\subseteq C^+$; $SO(V,\eta)=\{L:\det L=1\}$, $O^{\uparrow}(V,\eta)=\{L:L(C^+)=C^+\}$ and $SO^+(V,\eta)=SO(V,\eta)\cap O^{\uparrow}(V,\eta)$ are subgroups of $O(V,\eta)$, which is a subgroup of $GL(V)$; if $L$ is proper then $\epsilon(Lv_0,\dots,Lv_3)=\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)$ and if $\det L=-1$ the two sides differ by the sign $-1$ ([[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]], [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]).

[L3] For every $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ the passive boost $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with $B(\boldsymbol\beta)^{-1}=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$; the map $\boldsymbol\beta\mapsto B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is injective and $B(\mathbf 0)=\operatorname{id}_V$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]], [[def-lorentz-boost]]).

[L4] For every unit spatial vector $e$ and all $\beta_1,\beta_2\in(-1,1)$, $B(\beta_1e)B(\beta_2e)=B\bigl(\frac{\beta_1+\beta_2}{1+\beta_1\beta_2}e\bigr)$ with $\bigl|\frac{\beta_1+\beta_2}{1+\beta_1\beta_2}\bigr|<1$, and the two collinear boosts commute ([[lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition]]).

[L5] The map $r\mapsto\tanh(r)$ is a strictly increasing bijection of $\mathbb R$ onto $(-1,1)$, and for every unit spatial vector $e$ and all $r,s\in\mathbb R$ one has $B(\tanh(r)e)B(\tanh(s)e)=B(\tanh(r+s)e)$ ([[lem-rapidity-parametrization-of-collinear-boosts]]).

[L6] For a proper orthochronous Lorentz map $L$ with $u:=Le_0$ and coordinates $(u^0,u_{\mathrm{vec}})$, the parameter $\boldsymbol\beta:=u_{\mathrm{vec}}/u^0$ satisfies $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$, and $L=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$ with $\widehat R:=B(\boldsymbol\beta)L$ the extension $\operatorname{diag}(1,R)$ of a spatial rotation of the frame; this factorization is unique among parameters in the open unit ball and spatial rotations; conversely every such $B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$ is proper orthochronous; and $L$ is a passive boost if and only if $\widehat R=\operatorname{id}_V$ ([[lem-boost-rotation-factorization]]).

[L7] A spatial rotation of the frame is the extension by $e_0\mapsto e_0$ of a linear map of $S$ preserving $\delta$ with determinant $+1$ on $S$; its extension is denoted $\operatorname{diag}(1,R)$ in the frame's basis ([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]).

[L8] In the frame the timelike set is $T=T_+\cup T_-$ with $T_+=\{v:v^0>|v_{\mathrm{vec}}|\}$ and $T_-=\{v:v^0<-|v_{\mathrm{vec}}|\}$, and $T_+,T_-$ are exactly the two components; since $e_0\in C^+$ has coordinates $(1,0,0,0)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), one has $C^+=T_+$ and $C^-=T_-$, with closed cones $\operatorname{cl}(C^+)=\{v:v^0\ge|v_{\mathrm{vec}}|\}$ and $\operatorname{cl}(C^-)=\{v:v^0\le-|v_{\mathrm{vec}}|\}$ ([[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

[L9] A nonzero vector is timelike when $\eta(v,v)<0$, null when $\eta(v,v)=0$, spacelike when $\eta(v,v)>0$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); the oriented volume form satisfies $\epsilon_{0123}=+1$ ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]); $\det$ of a linear operator is the determinant of its matrix in any ordered basis and the Leibniz sum over a diagonal matrix is the product of its diagonal entries ([[def-determinant-of-a-linear-operator]], [[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]).

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a $4$-dimensional Lorentz vector space with time orientation

facts: [L1] Four-velocity and four-acceleration ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]): $U = x'/\tau'$ and, when $x$ is $C^{2}$, $A = U'/\tau'$; the dimensionless four-velocity is $u = U/c$.
[L2] Proper time ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]): $\tau'(s) = c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))} > 0$ everywhere, and $x'$ is future timelike.

[L7] Chart structure ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]): in an inertial chart $\eta_0 = \operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; the restriction $\delta$ of $\eta$ to $S = \operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is the Euclidean form with norm $|\cdot|$ and inner product written $w \cdot z := \delta(w,z)$; $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is a $\delta$-orthonormal basis.

[F1] In an inertial chart of the model, $\eta(u,v)=-u^0v^0+u^1v^1+u^2v^2+u^3v^3$, the tangent space at each event is canonically identified with $V$, and the flat covariant derivative acts on components by ordinary coordinate derivatives: $(
abla_XY)^a=X^b\partial_bY^a$. It is torsion-free, $

abla_YX=[X,Y]$; metric compatible, $
