abla_{[X,Y]}Z=0$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

[F2] Kinematics of the congruence: $\nabla_an_b=-n_aa_b+\theta_{ab}+\omega_{ab}$, with $a_b=\eta_{bc}a^c$ and $a=\nabla_nn$; $\theta$ is symmetric and $\omega$ antisymmetric; both are horizontal, $\theta_{ab}n^b=\omega_{ab}n^b=n^a\theta_{ab}=n^a\omega_{ab}=0$; $h=\eta+n^\flat\otimes n^\flat$ satisfies $h(v,w)=\eta(h(v),h(w))$ with $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$, its radical is spanned by $n$ and its restriction to $n^\perp$ is positive definite; Born rigidity is $\mathcal L_nh=0$, equivalently $\theta=0$; and $a^\flat(n)=0$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]], [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] clause (c), [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]).

[F3] Flow box and adapted charts: a smooth nowhere-zero vector field is locally $\partial/\partial u^0$ in suitable coordinates, and every observer congruence admits local adapted charts; in particular $n=\partial_s$ in coordinates $(s,y^1,y^2,y^3)$ on a flow box $U$, and the integral curves of $n$ are its $s$-lines ([[thm-flow-box-theorem]], [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]], [[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]]).

[F4] Connection one-forms and curvature two-forms: for a local frame $e_A$ with dual coframe $\theta^A$, the connection matrix $\gamma^A{}_B$ is defined by $\nabla_Xe_B=\gamma^A{}_B(X)e_A$, and the curvature two-forms satisfy $\Omega^A{}_B=d\gamma^A{}_B+\gamma^A{}_C\wedge\gamma^C{}_B$ with $R(X,Y)e_B=\Omega^A{}_B(X,Y)e_A$ ([[def-connection-one-form-in-a-local-frame]], [[thm-curvature-two-form-structure-equation]]). For the flat connection of [F1], $\Omega^A{}_B=0$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]], clause (c)).

[F7] Primitives: every closed smooth one-form on a star-shaped open domain has a smooth primitive, and every closed $C^1$ one-form on a nonempty path-connected simply connected open subset of $A$ has a $C^2$ primitive; a form is closed when $d\alpha=0$ ([[thm-poincare-lemma-for-differential-forms-on-star-shaped-domains]], [[lem-sr-closed-one-form-primitive-on-simply-connected-open-sets]], [[def-closed-and-exact-differential-forms]]).

[F11] Curves and integral curves: through every point of $\Omega$ there is a unique maximal integral curve of $n$, and a $C^1$ curve with $\gamma'=n\circ\gamma$ is smooth because $n$ is smooth and $s\mapsto n(\gamma(s))$ is then $C^1$, so $\gamma'$ is $C^1$ and $\gamma$ is $C^2$; iterating gives smoothness ([[def-integral-curve-of-a-vector-field]], [[thm-unique-maximal-integral-curve-through-each-point]], [[thm-chain-rule]], [[def-derivative]]). Every such maximal curve with $n$ future unit is a future timelike worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

[F13] Frobenius criterion for rest distributions: on an open set the rest distribution $\ker n^\flat$ is integrable if and only if $\omega=0$ there, if and only if $n^\flat\wedge d(n^\flat)=0$; when it is integrable, its integral hypersurfaces are the pointwise rest slices $n^\perp$ ([[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]], clause (iii)).

direct_context: **Given:** The affine Minkowski model with an inertial chart $x$ ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), a closed nondegenerate axis-parallel box $B=\prod_{a=0}^3[c_a,d_a]$, and a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field $T$ on an open neighbourhood $U\supseteq B$ ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]); the components $T^{ab}$ are $C^1$ functions on $U$ and $f^b=\partial_aT^{ab}$ with $\partial_a$ the coordinate partial derivatives. For a face $F_a^\pm$ of a box, its face integral is the Riemann integral of the restricted continuous function over the product of the remaining three coordinate intervals.

facts: [L1] The transition of two inertial charts is affine with linear part $\Lambda=M^{-1}$, the matrix of the proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map $L$ with $Le_a=e'_a$; the linear parts of transitions are exactly the proper orthochronous Lorentz matrices and their inverses ([[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]).

[L2] A linear Lorentz map is a linear isomorphism preserving $\eta$; its matrix in an orthonormal basis satisfies the metric condition; it is proper when its determinant is $+1$ and orthochronous when it maps $C^+$ onto $C^+$; the affine Lorentz maps form a group ([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]], [[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]]).

[L3] A $\mathcal C^k$ type-$(r,s)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ assigns to $p\in\Omega$ a multilinear $T(p):(V^*)^r\times V^s\to\mathbb R$, with components $T^{a_1\dots a_r}{}_{b_1\dots b_s}(p)=T(p)(e^{*a_1},\dots,e_{b_1},\dots)$ in a frame, and regularity is chart-independent ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], [[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]).

[L6] An alternating $k$-linear map is a $k$-linear map vanishing whenever two arguments coincide ([[def-alternating-k-linear-map]]); the oriented volume form of the model is $\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)=\det([v_j^a])$ in an inertial frame, an alternating $4$-linear form with $\epsilon_{0123}=+1$ ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]).

[L7] For a proper linear Lorentz map $L$ the oriented volume form satisfies $\epsilon(Lv_0,\dots,Lv_3)=\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)$, and for $\det L=-1$ the two sides differ by the sign $-1$ ([[lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure]]).

[L8] At $\boldsymbol\beta=\mathbf0$ the boost is the identity; the quotient expressions in clause (vi) and the proof are used only for nonzero $\boldsymbol\beta$, with their spatial correction interpreted as zero at $\boldsymbol\beta=\mathbf0$. The passive boost with parameter $\boldsymbol\beta$ has the coordinate action and matrix displayed in [[def-lorentz-boost]], with inverse $B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$, and $\gamma=(1-|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]]).

[L9] In an inertial chart, $x(p)=E^{-1}(p-o)$ with $E$ the coordinate isomorphism and $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). For the conditional coordinate-velocity interpretation in clause (vii), fix a real constant $c>0$ and define the reparametrized coordinate $t:=x^0/c$. This is a mathematical rescaling; no SI unit or physical-clock identification is assumed.
inverse_uses: [L1] The transition of two inertial charts is affine with linear part $\Lambda=M^{-1}$, the matrix of the proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map $L$ with $Le_a=e'_a$; the linear parts of transitions are exactly the proper orthochronous Lorentz matrices and their inverses ([[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]).

1.1 Write the transition as $x'^a=\Lambda^a{}_cx^c+b^a$ with $\Lambda$ invertible, $\det\Lambda=+1$ and $\Lambda$ orthochronous by [L1] and [L2]; the inverse relation is $x^c=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a(x'^a-b^a)$. By the chain rule [L12], wherever the derivatives exist, $\partial_c=\frac{\partial x'^a}{\partial x^c}\partial'_a=\Lambda^a{}_c\partial'_a$ and $\partial'_a=\frac{\partial x^c}{\partial x'^a}\partial_c=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a\partial_c$, and the two matrices are inverse: $\Lambda^a{}_c(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_d=\delta^a_d$ and $(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a\Lambda^a{}_d=\delta^c_d$ by [L12]. [L1, L2, L12, algebra, L10]

2.2 For the covector field, write $k=k_b\,dx^b$ and $k=k'_a\,dx'^a$; since $x^c=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a(x'^a-b^a)$, the chain rule [L12] gives $dx^c=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a\,dx'^a$, so $k=k_b(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_a\,dx'^a$ and comparing coefficients gives $k'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_ak_b$. For the phase function, substitute the inverse relation: $k_ax^a+\theta_0=k_a(\Lambda^{-1})^a{}_c(x'^c-b^c)+\theta_0=k'_cx'^c+\theta_0-k'_cb^c$, where the last step uses $k'_c=k_a(\Lambda^{-1})^a{}_c$; hence $\theta=k'_ax'^a+\theta'_0$ with $\theta'_0=\theta_0-k'_ab^a$, and the phase function has the same value at every event in both charts. This proves (ii). [L4, L12, step 1.1, algebra]

2.3 For the tensor law, [L1] gives $e'_a=Le_a$ with $L$ proper orthochronous and matrix $M$ satisfying $e'_a=M^b{}_ae_b$ with $M=\Lambda^{-1}$; consequently the dual bases satisfy $e'^{*a}=\Lambda^a{}_be^{*b}$ (both sides pair with $e'_c=\sum_b(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_ce_b$ to give $\delta^a_c$ by [L4] and the inverse relations of step 1.1). By the component definition of [L3] and multilinearity of $T(p)$, $T'^{a_1\dots a_r}{}_{b_1\dots b_s}=T(p)(e'^{*a_1},\dots,e'_{b_1},\dots)=\Lambda^{a_1}{}_{c_1}\cdots(\Lambda^{-1})^{d_1}{}_{b_1}\cdots T^{c_1\dots c_r}{}_{d_1\dots d_s}$, which is the displayed law. Contracting the first contravariant with the first covariant index in the transformed components gives $\Lambda^{a}{}_{c}(\Lambda^{-1})^{d}{}_{a}\cdots=\delta^d{}_c\cdots$, which is the contraction of the untransformed components; the remaining free indices retain their respective transformation factors, yielding precisely the component law of the same type-$(r-1,s-1)$ tensor $\operatorname{ctr}(T)$. Thus contraction is invariant as an intrinsic operation, as [L5] states; a fully contracted scalar has the same numerical value in both charts. For the metric, its components are $\eta_{ab}=\eta(e_a,e_b)$ in any frame, and by [L2] and [L1] $\eta'_{ab}=\eta(e'_a,e'_b)=\eta(Le_a,Le_b)=\eta(e_a,e_b)=\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ in every inertial frame. This proves (iii). [L1, L2, L3, L4, L5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For the derivative law, step 1.1 gives $\partial'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_a\partial_b$. For the divergence, (i) gives $J'^a=\Lambda^a{}_cJ^c$, so $\partial'_aJ'^a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_a\partial_b(\Lambda^a{}_cJ^c)=\delta^b{}_c\partial_bJ^c=\partial_aJ^a$, using the inverse relations of step 1.1 and the index rule of [L12]. For a type-$(2,0)$ field, (iii) gives $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$, hence $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^e{}_a\partial_e(\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd})=\delta^e{}_c\Lambda^b{}_d\partial_eT^{cd}=\Lambda^b{}_d\partial_aT^{ad}$. This proves (iv). [L12, step 1.1, step 2.3, algebra]

facts: [F2] Scalar-field equation and Hilbert tensor: the field equation of the model with potential $V$ is $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$, and the Hilbert tensor of the density with this $V$ is $T^{ab}=K[\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi-\eta^{ab}(\tfrac12\partial_d\varphi\partial^d\varphi+V(\varphi))]$. ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]], [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]])

[F3] Divergence identity: $\partial_aT^{ab}=K(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi))\partial^b\varphi$; consequently any solution of the field equation has conserved Hilbert tensor. ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]])

[L1] The rest form and projection: $h(v,w)=\eta(v,w)+\eta(n,v)\eta(n,w)=\eta(h(v),h(w))$ with $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$; $h$ is symmetric with radical spanned by $n$ and is positive definite on $n^\perp$; the congruence acceleration $a:=\nabla_nn$ satisfies $\eta(n,a)=0$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (a),(b)).

[L2] Kinematic decomposition and Born rigidity: $\nabla_an_b=-n_aa_b+\theta_{ab}+\omega_{ab}$ with $\theta_{ab}=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}n_{d)}$ symmetric and horizontal in both slots, $\theta_{ab}n^b=n^a\theta_{ab}=0$, and $(L_nh)_{ab}=2\theta_{ab}$; Born rigidity, defined by $L_nh=0$, is therefore equivalent to $\theta=0$ ([[def-sr-observer-congruence-and-kinematics]] (c),(d)).

[L3] In an inertial chart $\eta$ has constant components, $\partial_a\eta_{bc}=0$, and $(\nabla_XY)^a=X^b\partial_bY^a$; the same component formula and metric compatibility hold for $C^1$ data ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] (a),(c),(e)).

[L4] Derivatives of the components of a $C^1$ vector field $Y$ along a $C^1$ curve $y$ are ordinary derivatives, $(\nabla_{\dot y}Y)^a=\frac{d}{ds}(Y^a\circ y)$, and for $n$ future unit timelike the field $s\mapsto Y(y(s))$ is a $C^1$ field along $y$ ([[def-flat-covariant-derivative-on-affine-minkowski-space]] (d), [[def-vector-field-and-section-along-a-smooth-curve]]).

[L5] Rest projection identities: $h\circ h=h$, $\operatorname{im}h=n^\perp$, $\ker h=\operatorname{span}(n)$, $h(n)=0$, $\eta(n,h(v))=0$, $v=-\eta(n,v)n+h(v)$, and $w\mapsto\sqrt{\eta(w,w)}$ is a norm on $n^\perp$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c)).

[L6] Proper time: for a $C^1$ future timelike worldline $x$ one has $\tau(b)-\tau(a)=c^{-1}\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}\,du$; along a flow line of $n$ parametrized with tangent $x'=n$ this gives $d\tau/ds=1/c$, so $\partial_\tau=c\,\partial_s$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]]).

[L7] Four-velocity: $U=x'/\tau'=cx'/\sqrt{-\eta(x',x')}$; for a congruence flow line with $x'=n$ this is $U=cn$, and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]] (a),(c), [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (a)).

[L8] Tensoriality: under an inertial chart change $x'=\Lambda x+b$ one has $J'^a=\Lambda^a_bJ^b$, $k'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b_ak_b$, $\partial'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b_a\partial_b$, and each contravariant index gains $\Lambda$ while each covariant index gains $\Lambda^{-1}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (i)-(iv)).

[L13] Smooth fields: the Lie bracket of smooth vector fields has coordinate components $[X,Y]^a=X^b\partial_bY^a-Y^b\partial_bX^a$, and for smooth data the coordinate expression of the Lie derivative of the covariant field $h$ is $n^c\partial_ch_{ab}+h_{cb}\partial_an^c+h_{ac}\partial_bn^c$ ([[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], [[prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-lie-bracket]], [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

[L15] Model structure: $T_pA$ is canonically identified with $V$, so the differential of a map into $A$ may be read as a $V$-valued derivative ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]).

[F1] Rest-space projector. The map $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ is linear and idempotent, has image $n^\perp$ and kernel $\operatorname{span}(n)$, satisfies $h(n)=0$ and $\eta(n,h(v))=0$ for all $v$; in components $h^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b$, so $h^a{}_bn^b=0=n_a h^a{}_b$ and $h^a{}_ch^c{}_b=h^a{}_b$. ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c))
[F2] Component conventions and symmetry: $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$, $\delta^a{}_b=h^a{}_b-n^an_b$, and index lowering commutes with the algebra. ([[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]])

[F1] Compactly supported differentiation under the integral sign: if $F:(-s_0,s_0)\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is continuous with continuous $\partial_sF$ and there is a compact $K\Subset\Omega$ with $F(s,z)=0$ for $z\notin K$ and all $s$, then $s\mapsto\int_\Omega F(s,z)\,d^4z$ is $C^1$ on $(-s_0,s_0)$ with derivative $\int_\Omega\partial_sF(s,z)\,d^4z$. ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(c))

[F2] Fundamental lemma: if $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and $\int_\Omega g\psi\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth compactly supported $\psi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, then $g=0$ on $\Omega$. ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(a))
inverse_uses: 1.1 Fix a smooth symmetric compactly supported $(0,2)$ field $h$ and set $g_{ab}(s,x):=\eta_{ab}+s\,h_{ab}(x)$ for $s\in\mathbb R$, $x\in\Omega$. Since $h_{ab}=0$ off $\operatorname{supp}h$, one has $g(s,x)=\eta$ off $\operatorname{supp}h$. The function $(s,x)\mapsto\det g(s,x)$ is, by [F3], a polynomial in $s$ with coefficients continuous in $x$ and equals $-1$ at $s=0$; for each $x$ continuity in $(s,x')$ at $(0,x)$ yields $\varepsilon(x)>0$ and a neighbourhood $U(x)$ of $x$ with $\det g(s,x')<0$ for $|s|<\varepsilon(x)$, $x'\in U(x)$, and compactness of $\operatorname{supp}h$ gives finitely many such sets and a common $s_0>0$ with $\det g(s,x)<0$ for all $|s|<s_0$, $x\in\Omega$. Hence for $|s|<s_0$ the matrix $g(s,x)$ is invertible, its inverse entries are $g^{ab}(s,x)=\det(g(s,x))^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(g(s,x))^{ab}$ by [F4], and $D_h(s,x):=[\tfrac12g^{ab}(s,x)\partial_a\varphi\partial_b\varphi+V(\varphi)]\sqrt{-\det g(s,x)}$ is defined; the maps $(s,x)\mapsto g^{ab}(s,x)$ and $(s,x)\mapsto\det g(s,x)$, being polynomials in the continuous entries and quotients with nowhere-vanishing denominator $\det g$, are continuous on $(-s_0,s_0)\times\Omega$ by [F7], and so are $\sqrt{-\det g(s,x)}$ by [F5] and $D_h(s,x)$ by [F7], and $D_h(s,x)=D_h(0,x)$ whenever $h_{ab}(x)=0$, in particular off $\operatorname{supp}h$. [given, F3, F4, F7]
